French actor Gérard ​Depardieu will face trial on charges of raping actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018, his lawyer said on ​Thursday. Depardieu, one of the leading faces of French ​cinema, has denied wrongdoing in the case.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/567ddbca-e219-11f1-90ba-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25086306397512.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/567ddbca-e219-11f1-90ba-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25086306397512.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">41d56940-e99e-11f1-b07b-7b879c10b60a</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:44:02 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/567ddbca-e219-11f1-90ba-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25086306397512.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>Housing crisis on the ballot: Anger boils over ahead of Spanish election</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20261126-housing-crisis-on-the-ballot-anger-boils-over-ahead-of-spanish-election</link><description>
Spaniards head to the polls on Sunday in a general election that was called after street protests for affordable housing. Anger bubbled over after 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal was evicted from her home of seven decades and two decrees to tackle the housing crisis were rejected by parliament. In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8fad2a10-e99c-11f1-be69-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a49da062.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8fad2a10-e99c-11f1-be69-1991d4929b54/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-a49da062.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e0a5da54-e8fa-11f1-bd51-89765fe8c5bf</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:33:21 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Maude Petit-Jové</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title><![CDATA['Europe has two kinds of countries: Small countries & those that haven’t yet realised they’re small’]]></title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/europe-has-two-kinds-of-countries-small-countries-those-that-haven-t-yet-realised-they-re-small</link><description>
“The implications of having the far right in power in Brussels are enormous,” warns Sophie Pornschlegel, Senior Advisor at the European Policy Centre. With elections approaching in several EU member states, including France and Italy, what would a growing number of far-right, Eurosceptic governments mean for the EU budget, relations between European institutions, common legislation and support for Ukraine? Could Giorgia Meloni could adopt a more radical stance? “The whole idea of the EU is to have a common legislation that is then applied in 27 member states. Otherwise, what is the point of having the EU?”
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa874ada-e994-11f1-97fb-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261126-080650-081732-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa874ada-e994-11f1-97fb-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261126-080650-081732-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0002fdce-e995-11f1-9cb2-21ab8fbc63ca</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:31:58 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261126-as-humans-we-feel-spiritually-homeless-turkish-author-ece-temelkuran-on-belonging</link><description>
For Ece Temelkuran, the human condition is "unhomed". Speaking to FRANCE 24, the Turkish author cites the rise of artificial intelligence, climate change and the authoritarian drift as reasons why one may no longer recognise the place one calls home. Most of all, she highlights the importance of human connection: "In survival mode (...) you live on the kindness of others."
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e1e4e52-e997-11f1-8567-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-2dfeb495.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e1e4e52-e997-11f1-8567-77d069279b82/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-2dfeb495.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">d384b0a8-e980-11f1-8c9f-998286d96f2c</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:48:46 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Carys GARLAND</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Thanksgiving night sky 2026 — What to look for after dinner tonight ]]> If your household is like most American families, then on Thursday you likely will all be sitting down with family and friends for a traditional Thanksgiving turkey dinner during the mid-to-late afternoon hours.

Then as darkness falls, some will probably migrate into the living room to catch some football or other holiday fare on television. But if you have a large gathering of family and friends at your home — and if your skies are mainly clear — why not invite everyone outside to gaze at the evening sky?

If you have binoculars, or better yet, a telescope, you just might end up turning this into a memorable family tradition of its own.

First, the "Lord of the Rings" . . .

If I may paraphrase the mysterious voice from the 1989 movie, "Field of Dreams": "If you set up your telescope, they will come." And you'll get a big kick out of your Turkey Day guests uttering all the "oohs" and "ahs" or exclamations of "Wow!" with just one peek through the eyepiece.

As darkness falls, Saturn will glow at first magnitude, shining with a sedate, yellow-white light and appearing noticeably brighter than the star Fomalhaut, about 40 degrees (the equivalent of four fist-widths) to its lower right.

Its famous ring system is now tilted only about six degrees toward Earth but may be visible with steadied (or image-stabilized) high-power binoculars or through the eyepiece of a telescope magnifying over 30-power. The rings will seem to glow with an inner light and for those who have never had the pleasure of seeing them for themselves, that first view always elicits astonishment; kids especially most often will say: "Awesome!" or "No way!" I've even had people accuse me of using a slide of Saturn, to which I, of course, reply with, "No . . . that's the real thing."

. . . and later, the moon

Then, along about 6:25 p.m. local time, the waning gibbous moon, 2½ days past full phase and 91% illuminated, will begin to emerge from beyond the east-northeast horizon. Give it another hour and it will stand about 10 degrees above the horizon — equal to the width of your clenched fist held at arm's length. By then, the moon will be in a better position for evening study.

Even in binoculars, the moon is a striking sight to see. It's such a special object because it doesn't matter whether you live in a rural area or in the middle of a brightly lit city, for the moon can always be readily observed. It always looks spectacular whether you're using binoculars or a telescope. It never looks precisely the same no matter how often you view it and can be observed even on hazy or partially cloud-covered nights.

Pay particular attention to the line of darkness — called the terminator — features near that border stand out in bold relief; the shadows become stronger and details are more easily seen. Take note on this night of the circular dark area, bisected by the terminator: Mare Crisium — the "Sea of Crises." Immediately bordering above it is a 50-mile (80 km)-wide ring of very rugged mountains, rising as high as 14,400 feet (4,389 meters), which now resembles a huge crater partially in shadow when the sun is low.

A bonus: A view of the International Space Station

Probably the one object that your Thanksgiving guests will want to see is the biggest and brightest of all the man-made objects orbiting the Earth: the International Space Station (ISS). Except for those living across the southern US, for most everywhere else, the ISS will be making visible passes on Thanksgiving evening.


Circling the Earth at an average altitude of 260 miles (420 km) and at a speed of 17,500 mph (28,200 kph), it can appear to move as fast as a high-flying jet airliner, sometimes taking as much as six or seven minutes to cross the sky. It can easily be confused with aircraft lights. Nominally, it appears white with a slight yellow tinge and at its very brightest it can sometimes appear to shine as bright as magnitude -5.6, which is twice as bright as the planet Venus!

So, what is the viewing schedule on Thanksgiving for your hometown? You can easily find out by visiting one of three popular websites:

Spot the Station

This site will tell you when and where to sight the ISS. All you need do is type in your city or town, then click on the map pinpoint to get all the details. You can even sign up to get email or text alerts when the space station is flying over.

Chris Peat's Heavens Above

This site will not only provide you with sighting information for the ISS, but also for many other satellites as well. You must first register and then you can input your location to generate a sighting schedule.

Live Real-Time Satellite Tracking

Like Heavens Above, you can get sighting information for the ISS and other satellites. Once you log on this site will automatically provide details based on your IP address ... or you can set a "custom" location.

Here at Space.com, we like to wish a very happy and safe Thanksgiving to all, and of course, clear skies!

Joe Rao serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky and Telescope, The Old Farmer's Almanac and other publications.

]]> <![CDATA[ Space plants with hot sauce: What ISS astronauts will be eating on Thanksgiving (video) ]]>

The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare.

Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens.

"We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base, and as we go to Mars, we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video.

"I plan on using this [plant] with a tortilla and some pasta and some hot sauce to make my Thanksgiving meal," added Menon, who was wearing a chef's toque for the occasion. "And I'm grateful for you and for my family at home."

He passed the microphone to fellow NASA astronaut Luke Delaney, who didn't talk about food but expressed gratitude to his family, crewmates and support network on Earth.

Next up was NASA's Jessica Watkins, who gave us a rundown of the broader Thanksgiving menu in space.

"Some of what we'll be eating here — we've got some roasted turkey, some mac and cheese, some mashed potatoes, and some candied yams," Watkins said, showing off the small bags containing each of those comestibles. "So, we should be in good shape."

The Canadian Space Agency's (CSA) Joshua Kutryk spoke next. He said he'll eat rice and the space-grown plants, which he'll consume raw "because it reminds me of Earth, which I miss."

All four of the astronauts then wished us a happy Thanksgiving and did some zero-g flips and rolls, sending the space plants on a bit of a ride.

Delaney, Kutryk and Watkins are members of SpaceX's Crew-13 mission, which arrived at the International Space Station (ISS) on Oct. 1. There's a fourth Crew-13 astronaut as well — Sergey Teteryatnikov, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos.

That quartet shares the ISS with Menon and cosmonauts Pyotr Dubrov and Anna Kikina, who arrived in July aboard a Russian Soyuz spacecraft.

Astronauts tend to get major holidays off on the ISS, and to celebrate them together. Doing so reinforces the already-strong bonds the crewmates share and helps them deal with the pain of being away from friends and family, which can be especially acute on holidays like Thanksgiving and Christmas.

Kutryk is likely feeling especially emotional these days. On Tuesday, the CSA announced that Kutryk's wife had given birth to the couple's third child, a daughter.

"Even with the distance between us, we feel incredibly connected as we welcome our new little star into our lives," the couple said in a statement shared by the CSA. "We are very proud of our growing family and are looking forward to getting our little crew of five all reunited."

On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight.

The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft.

After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights.

The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet.

Why it mattered

In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind.

In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body, after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said.

"When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview.

Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation.

"A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote. "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft."

If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C.

When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived.

Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print.

The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time.

Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above.

Monuments

Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik.

In that hand is a piece of hardware Malik remembers watching Massimino wrestle with in real time. During NASA's final Hubble servicing mission in 2009, a stripped bolt left a handrail blocking access to the telescope's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS). Mission Control instructed Massimino to forcibly remove the handrail so he and fellow spacewalker Michael Good could get on with the repair.

Massimino told Malik that pulling the handrail off Hubble brought back a childhood memory of his father and his Uncle Frank driving a long screwdriver through a stuck oil filter. "Then my uncle Frank pulled to get more leverage, and that's what was going through my mind when I pulled off that handrail," Massimino said. He remembered looking down at Earth and thinking, "This one's for you, Uncle Frank."

Massimino wore bulky, pressurized gloves to pull off the handrail, but Zelinskie chose to show his bare hand gripping the copper-plated replica. "I wanted to bring the humanity back into the piece," she told Malik.

The gloves have a story of their own. When Massimino brought a pair to her studio to be 3D-scanned, Zelinskie noticed how the fabric held its folds when the gloves were set down. "Oh my god, these want to be stone," she recalled thinking. So she went out and learned to work in marble.

The astronaut boots have a detail you could easily miss from above. Zelinskie polished the soles smooth because, as she put it, "they're built for floating in space." For her sculpture of Massimino's reentry helmet, the kind he wore for the trip home from space, Zelinskie paired carved marble with a 3D-printed visor, which she electroplated and polished to a mirror finish.

The Hubble Space Telescope gets its own marble tribute in "Monuments." Zelinskie started with a NASA 3D model of the telescope and used the modeling software Blender to give it a veil.

"So I kind of threw a digital piece of fabric on the Hubble telescope over and over and over again until I got it right," she told Malik. The veil is a nod to the blurry images Hubble first sent back to Earth. A Digital Stone Project robotic arm in Tuscany carved the rough shape in marble, and Zelinskie finished it by hand. When she invited Malik to touch what looked like cloth, he reached out. "It's like a very buttery, smooth surface," he said.

The last time we saw Zelinskie at Heft, she and DJ and producer illich Mujica had filled the gallery with Webb imagery, live electronic music and a little Pink Floyd for their audiovisual performance "Redshift." We've also seen her turn Webb's view of the Pillars of Creation into artwork. This time, one of the images on the wall began with a camera Zelinskie pointed at a rocket herself.

Zelinskie photographed NASA's Artemis 2 launch from the Kennedy Space Center visitor center in Florida. The resulting print is part of "Ejecta," alongside the Starship breakup print and more. She uses data to distort the image until the swirls in a rocket plume start to resemble a nebula.

The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. "This is the kind of American ingenuity that can unite our strengths in space and advanced technology, reinforce our economic leadership, and expand prosperity here at home."

Poslanec Jindřich Rajchl (PRO, zvolený za vládní SPD) připravuje změnu trestního zákoníku, která by omezila možnosti trestně postihovat jejich veřejné popírání, zpochybňování nebo schvalování. Kde je hranice mezi svobodným vyjadřováním názorů a trestným činem? Stávající zákon v Česku takové jednání postihuje bez nutnosti prokazovat podněcování k nenávisti nebo násilí, čímž to chce Rajchl nově podmínit.    <title>Chřipka už se v Česku rozjela. Odborníci řekli, kdy letos očekávat epidemii</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/zdravotnictvi/chripka-se-uz-rozjela-epidemii-odbornici-ocekavaji-pred-vanocemi/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zdravotnictvi</link>
   <description>Chřipka je tu. Její větší záchyty zaznamenali odborníci o něco dřív než v uplynulých letech. I její epidemii proto očekávají s předstihem, zřejmě již před Vánocemi. Na očkování zatím ale podle nich není pozdě. Je však dobré s ním příliš neotálet, neboť dotyčného začíná chránit až po dvou týdnech. Vakcinaci doporučují především starším lidem, chronicky nemocným, těhotným ženám či zdravotnickým pracovníkům.</description>

   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesi-v-cislech/zaplatili-zbozi-nikde-kazdy-jedenacty-cech-prisel-pri-on-line-nakupu-o-penize/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesi-v-cislech</link>
   <description>Při nákupu na internetu stačí pár kliknutí a objednávka je na cestě. Už tento pátek přichází Black Friday, který láká na mimořádně výhodné nabídky. Ne všechny jsou však skutečné. Zvlášť u obchodu, kde člověk nakupuje poprvé, může být těžké odhadnout, komu svěřuje své peníze. Na to, jak si lidé e-shopy prověřují a jaké zkušenosti mají s nepovedenými nákupy, se zaměřila datová redakce Deníku.cz.</description>

   <title>Vrchní soud požádal Senát o vydání Martina Půty k trestnímu stíhání </title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/vrchni-soud-pozadal-senat-o-vydani-martina-puty-k-trestnimu-stihani/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Vrchní soud v Praze požádal Senát o vydání senátora za Českolipsko a libereckého hejtmana Martina Půty (Starostové pro Liberecký kraj) k trestnímu stíhání. Půta to dnes uvedl na síti X. Doplnil, že již před druhým kolem senátních voleb, ve kterých byl zvolen, avizoval, že bude s vydáním souhlasit. Půta byl nepravomocně odsouzen za to, že formou protislužby přijal úplatek 30 000 korun a jednal ve prospěch svého známého. Vinu odmítá.</description>

      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/new-york-odlozil-pruvod-den-dikuvzdani-100-let-boure.A261126_135132_zahranicni_vanky#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Jubilejní 100. ročník slavného průvodu společnosti Macy’s na Den díkůvzdání se v New Yorku ve čtvrtek neuskuteční. Kvůli očekávané silné pobřežní bouři s nárazy větru až 105 kilometrů za hodinu a rizikem záplav ho radnice s organizátory odložila na sobotu 28. listopadu. Jde o historicky první přesun průvodu kvůli počasí od jeho založení v roce 1924.</description>

      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ostrava/zpravy/vanoce-opava-ruske-kolo-zruseni-atrakce-vanocni-trhy-czudek-kritika.A261126_122457_ostrava-zpravy_dmk#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Bouřlivou diskusi spustilo v Opavě zdůvodnění toho, že součástí letošních vánočních trhů nebude ruské kolo. Pomoci může pestrý jídelníček, pohyb i kvalitní spánek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906715-podzim-proveri-vasi-imunitu-pomoci-muze-pestry-jidelnicek-pohyb-i-kvalitni-spanek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906715-podzim-proveri-vasi-imunitu-pomoci-muze-pestry-jidelnicek-pohyb-i-kvalitni-spanek.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Chladné počasí, méně slunce a období zvýšeného výskytu respiračních infekcí představují pro lidský organismus větší zátěž. Obranyschopnost přitom můžeme podpořit i běžnými každodenními návyky. Důležitou roli hraje především pestrá strava, dostatek spánku, pravidelný pohyb a péče o střevní mikrobiom.</description></item><item><title>Přepadení v Jablonci. Útočník udeřil zezadu prodavačku, za hodinu už seděl v cele</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906781-prepadeni-v-jablonci-utocnik-uderil-zezadu-prodavacku-za-hodinu-uz-sedel-v-cele.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906781-prepadeni-v-jablonci-utocnik-uderil-zezadu-prodavacku-za-hodinu-uz-sedel-v-cele.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Útok na prodavačku v jablonecké prodejně skončil bleskovým dopadením pachatele. Muž ženu napadl zezadu kvůli nákupu za pár stovek, ale z lupu se dlouho netěšil – policisté ho chytili necelou hodinu po činu a soudce ho poslal rovnou do vazby.</description></item><item><title>Důvěra ve veřejnoprávní média se liší podle vzdělání. Výzkum odhalil další souvislosti</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906745-duvera-ve-verejnopravni-media-se-lisi-podle-vzdelani-vyzkum-odhalil-dalsi-souvislosti.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906745-duvera-ve-verejnopravni-media-se-lisi-podle-vzdelani-vyzkum-odhalil-dalsi-souvislosti.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 10:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Michael Daněk</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>České televizi, Českému rozhlasu a České tiskové kanceláři důvěřuje téměř polovina české populace. Vyplývá to z dlouhodobého výzkumu Psychologického ústavu Akademie věd ČR a agentury Median, podle kterého velmi nebo spíše důvěřuje veřejnoprávním médiím 48 procent respondentů.</description></item><item><title>Od šelem až do pralesa: Zoo a botanickou propojí v sobotu zážitková stezka</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906741-od-selem-az-do-pralesa-zoologickou-a-botanickou-zahradu-propoji-v-sobotu-stezka.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906741-od-selem-az-do-pralesa-zoologickou-a-botanickou-zahradu-propoji-v-sobotu-stezka.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:20:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V sobotu 28. listopadu čeká rodiny s dětmi v Liberci netradiční dobrodružství. Zážitková stezka plná úkolů propojí zdejší zoologickou a botanickou zahradu. Výprava odstartuje mezi zvířaty v zoo, povede lesíkem a vyvrcholí v tropických sklenících botanické zahrady.</description></item><item><title>V republice kolem nuly, v Liberci mráz. Výstraha na sníh v kraji tentokrát neplatí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906738-v-republice-kolem-nuly-v-liberci-mraz-vystraha-na-snih-v-kraji-tentokrat-neplati.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906738-v-republice-kolem-nuly-v-liberci-mraz-vystraha-na-snih-v-kraji-tentokrat-neplati.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 07:51:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zatímco jinde v republice byly noční teploty jen kolem nuly, v Libereckém kraji klesly hluboko pod bod mrazu. V Liberci bylo k ránu až -10 stupňů Celsia a na Jizerce dokonce teplota klesla na -15 stupňů. Meteorologická výstraha před silným sněžením se Libereckého kraje tentokrát netýká.</description></item><item><title>Soud požádal Senát o vydání Půty k trestnímu stíhání</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906734-soud-pozadal-senat-o-vydani-puty-k-trestnimu-stihani.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/906734-soud-pozadal-senat-o-vydani-puty-k-trestnimu-stihani.html</guid><pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 06:26:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Vrchní soud v Praze požádal Senát o vydání senátora a libereckého hejtmana Martina Půty (Starostové pro Liberecký kraj) k trestnímu stíhání. Půta to uvedl na síti X. Doplnil, že již před druhým kolem senátních voleb, ve kterých byl zvolen, avizoval, že bude s vydáním souhlasit.</description></item><item><title>Domácností s dětmi v EU ubývá. Česko je nad průměrem, porodnost ale padá</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906454-domacnosti-s-detmi-v-eu-ubyva-cesko-je-nad-prumerem-porodnost-ale-pada.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906454-domacnosti-s-detmi-v-eu-ubyva-cesko-je-nad-prumerem-porodnost-ale-pada.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 19:56:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Jiří Komárek</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Domácností s dětmi v Evropské unii dlouhodobě ubývá. Podle dat, která Eurostat zveřejnil 20. listopadu, v roce 2025 nežily děti mladší 18 let v 76,6 % evropských domácností. Podíl domácností s dětmi klesá bez přerušení: v roce 2010 činil 26,9 %, loňského roku už pouze 23,3 %.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký kraj bude sčítat návštěvníky Ještědu, cílem je udržitelný turismus</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906660-liberecky-kraj-bude-scitat-navstevniky-jestedu-cilem-je-udrzitelny.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906660-liberecky-kraj-bude-scitat-navstevniky-jestedu-cilem-je-udrzitelny.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 18:20:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj bude sčítat návštěvníky Ještědu. Projekt souvisí s plány kraje na zapsání horského hotelu a vysílače na jeho vrcholu na Seznam světového dědictví UNESCO. Cílem je udržitelný turismus, který nebude poškozovat památkově chráněnou budovu ani její okolí.</description></item><item><title>Advent ve Fabrice se vrací s pestrým programem a kouzelnou vánoční atmosférou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906528-advent-ve-fabrice-se-vraci-s-pestrym-programem-a-kouzelnou-vanocni-atmosferou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906528-advent-ve-fabrice-se-vraci-s-pestrym-programem-a-kouzelnou-vanocni-atmosferou.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:54:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Po úspěšném prvním ročníku se do semilské FABRIKY 1861 vrací Advent ve Fabrice. Od 29. listopadu do 20. prosince nabídne každou neděli od 13.00 do 18.00 hodin vánoční trhy, koncerty, loutková divadla, komentované prohlídky i letošní novinky.</description></item><item><title>Falešný průkaz koně i pas Antarktidy. Padělané doklady sbírají policisté jako Pokémony</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906645-falesny-prukaz-kone-i-pas-antarktidy-padelane-doklady-sbiraji-policiste-jako-pokemony.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906645-falesny-prukaz-kone-i-pas-antarktidy-padelane-doklady-sbiraji-policiste-jako-pokemony.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 15:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Eva Hradilová</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Už deset let sbírají experti z Národního centra pro kontrolu dokladů dokumenty, které pocházejí z dílen padělatelů. Odhalili jich skoro 14 tisíc, pět tisíc z nich si nechali v archivu. Jsou tam třeba průkazy astrálních bytostí, falešný průkaz koně nebo diplomatický pas Antarktidy.</description></item></channel></rss>

]]> Ezagutu Lužice aneb Poznejte Lužici https://www.vybezek.eu/297720-ezagutu-luzice-aneb-poznejte-luzici/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:23:04 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297720 Literárně naučné miniturné po Čechách lužickosrbské spisovatelky Róži Domašcyny, básníka a překladatele Milana Hrabala a hudebníka Vojtěcha Kouby.

Ve dnech 3. a 4. listopadu 2026 proběhly dva večery věnované lužickosrbské literatuře a kultuře pod názvem Ezagutu Lužice (Poznejte Lužici), které pořádaly, ruku v ruce, nakladatelství Euskaldun a Společnost přátel Lužice. Nejednalo se o první takovou spolupráci, ale o vyvrcholení celého cyklu pořadů věnovaným menším jazykovým skupinám bez vlastní státnosti, které jsou nějakým způsobem svázány s českými zeměmi. První večer proběhl v Plzni v univerzitní kavárně Družba a následující den se přesunul takříkajíc na domácí hřiště do pražského Lužického semináře.

Hlavními hvězdami večerů byly Róža Domašcyna, jedna z nejvýznamnějších lužickosrbských autorek a Milan Hrabal, básník, překladatel, přítel a propagátor Lužice. O hudební doprovod se postaral Vojtěch Kouba, který představil publiku lužický folklór, ale zároveň i vlastní tvorbu.

Na první večer dorazilo asi čtyřicet zvídavých Plzeňanů, pro které bylo setkání s literaturou a historií nejmenšího západoslovanského národa iniciačním zážitkem. Milan Hrabal se ukázal, jako výborný průvodce lužicko-srbskými reáliemi i historií. Navíc bavil publikum tím, jak se postupně přiznával k různým překladatelským přehmatům. Poezie Róži Domašcyny a písně Vojtěcha Kouby vykouzlily čarovnou atmosféru jak v plzeňské studentské kavárně, tak pod barokní klenbou Lužického semináře.

Sychravé počasí za okny kontrastovalo s vřelou a neformální atmosférou obou večerů. U srdce zahřály i reakce návštěvníků. Etablovaný plzeňský básník Jan Sojka poklekl před organizátory večera na kolena, líbal jim ruce a děkoval za krásný večer. Herpetolog Ondřej Škach zase prohlásil, že nelituje toho, že vyměnil oslavu úspěšného odchovu zmije pavoučí v plzeňské ZOO, za lužickosrbský večer, neboť o zmijích ví všechno, ale o Lužici nevěděl doposud nic. Filolog Mikuláš Liptovský se nechal výkonem účinkujících dokonce strhnout ke slibu, že se na stará kolena pustí do studia sorabistiky. Studenty pražských uměleckých škol zase okouzlil Milan Hrabal natolik, že se zajímali o to, kdy bude mít v Lužickém semináři příští seminář o Lužici. Není divu, že se návštěvníci nechali vtáhnout do průběhu večera. Byl totiž úplně jiný, než obvykle literární večery bývají. Domašcyna s Hrabalem jsou na sebe mentálně navázaní a je na jejich vystoupení znát, že jsou sehraná dvojice. Kouba je pak skvěle doplňuje svými písněmi. Většina diváků slyšela asi poprvé dylanovku v lužické srbštině.  O pozitivních pocitech publika svědčí i ovace ve stoje, které následovaly po pražském večeru.

V době, kdy některé vlády vedou kulturní války proti vlastním občanům, tito se jim staví literaturou a radostí, kterou přináší umění slova. Je hezké vidět, když se lidé sejdou, aby vyslechli hlas malého národa a tím se o něco víc přiblížili ke břehům ostrova zapomenutých.

Martin Holý , Euskaldun
